title: Cross-env escalation: hotpatch idempotency sanitizer and telemetry fingerprint
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: A customer escalation (tenant T-842) exposed intermittent 5xx waves and long tail timeouts across Hosted and Dedicated routing during a migration window. Symptoms suggested a replay/retry amplification combined with stale KV-cache entries causing model server responses to return transient 5xxs and downstream timeouts. This ticket contains a safety hotpatch (idempotency sanitizer + request telemetry fingerprint) and a follow-up reconciliation job to restore KV consistency.

Why different from prior work: previous incidents centered on proxy retry coordination and tenant shaping. This event appears to be cross-environment: an SDK mismatch in a Dedicated migration path produced badly-formed idempotency keys which led to collision and cache pollution. The mitigation is therefore two-pronged: (1) canonicalize and sanitize idempotency keys at the edge to prevent collisions and accidental reuse; (2) emit a compact telemetry fingerprint per request to detect replay storms and correlate across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to enable rapid tenant-scoped mitigation and forensics.

Goals: 1) stop ongoing customer-visible 5xx waves and timeout amplification for T-842; 2) ensure fixes are safe to roll out to Hosted without regressions for other tenants; 3) detect similar patterns proactively via the new fingerprint metric.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate the customer migration path from Dedicated -> Hosted via the migration proxy shim.
2) Use SDK v0.9.3 (the older client) which omits a tenant prefix when generating idempotency keys.
3) Send a burst of identical requests (same prompt, varying attachments) with short retry windows from 50 concurrent connections and default client retries enabled.
4) Observe KV cache entries with conflicting keys and a small fraction of responses returning 5xx when the model backend hits a corrupted cache key.
5) Confirm amplification when client retries reuse the same malformed idempotency key instead of a fresh one.

mitigation_applied:
- Tenant T-842 admitted to a temporary rate-floor and queued non-essential requests.
- Edge activated request fingerprinting for tracing correlated retries.
- Canary of idempotency sanitizer (edge-level middleware) deployed to edge-3 and edge-4. The sanitizer rewrites client idempotency keys into: SHA256(tenant_id || route || canonicalized_idempotency_key) and rejects collisions where hash maps to multiple active sessions.
- Added a short-lived compatibility shim to map older SDK keys (v0.9.2/0.9.3 patterns) to canonicalized form to avoid breaking in-flight clients.
resolution_plan:
Phase 1 (hotfix): Ship idempotency sanitizer to all edge nodes behind feature flag; enable telemetry fingerprint globally; expand tenant admission control automation.
Phase 2 (reconciliation): Run KV-cache reconciliation job that scans for suspicious keys (matching old SDK fingerprint patterns) and repairs or evicts corrupted entries with a low-impact throttle.
Phase 3 (preventive): Publish SDK guidance, add server-side validation for idempotency key entropy and prefixing, and add automated alerting that triggers when fingerprint replay ratio > 0.5 for a tenant.
Phase 4 (postmortem): Complete incident review and update runbooks with cross-env migration checklist and SDK compatibility gating.
rollout_plan:
- Canary: edge-3 (1% traffic) for 2h, verify 5xx rate and fingerprint-replay decrease.
- Expand to edges [edge-1, edge-2, edge-4] over 6 hours if metrics stable.
- Enable tenant admission automation for all tenants after 24h of stable telemetry.
- If errors trend up after rollout, automatic rollback via feature-flag with 5-minute safety gate.
- Notify customer success and affected customers at each milestone (canary pass/fail, full rollout).
test_plan:
- Unit: sanitizer canonicalization tests for a matrix of idempotency key formats (old SDK, new SDK, intentionally malformed).
- Integration: end-to-end request flow through proxy shim with synthetic replay bursts and validation that sanitizer prevents collisions and that backend KV behavior is non-destructive.
- Load: 500rps synthetic workload with expected retry patterns to ensure latency tail doesn't regress more than 5%.
- Post-deploy: automated check comparing fingerprint replay ratio against baseline for 24h.

notes:
Novelty: using a compact, reproducible telemetry fingerprint (tenant_id | route | model | prompt_hash | kv_version) lets us correlate across Hosted/Dedicated/Private routing layers. This produced a fast signal that the problem was cross-environment rather than pure backend instability.
Operational guidance: if a tenant migration is planned, ensure SDK and migration shim run compatibility tests that validate idempotency key format and entropy.
Follow-ups: add a compatibility check in the Dedicated migration runner that refuses migration if >1% of requests use legacy idempotency key patterns.
final_resolution: In progress — hotpatch rolled, reconciliation job scheduled; waiting on reconciliation completion and customer sign-off for closure.
